about.title: About Retirement Calculator
about.description: The Retirement Calculator helps you estimate how current savings, contributions, time horizon, and assumed returns may affect retirement planning. It can be used to review different contribution levels, retirement ages, and income goals so you can compare scenarios and identify possible gaps. Use it as a planning reference rather than a guarantee of future retirement outcomes.

howTo.title: How to Use the Retirement Calculator

steps.title: Enter Personal Information
steps.description: Input your current age and desired retirement age to establish your planning timeline.

steps.title: Add Current Savings
steps.description: Enter your current retirement savings balance across all accounts including 401(k), IRA, and other retirement funds.

steps.title: Set Contribution Amount
steps.description: Specify your expected annual contribution amount to retirement accounts.

steps.title: Expected Returns
steps.description: Input your expected annual rate of return (typically 6-8% for diversified portfolios).

steps.title: Retirement Income Goal
steps.description: Enter your desired annual retirement income to maintain your lifestyle.

steps.title: Review Results
steps.description: Review the projection and adjust parameters to compare retirement planning scenarios.

faq.q: How much should I save for retirement?
faq.a: Some planning frameworks use savings targets such as 10-15% of income, but the amount depends on your retirement goals, current age, expected lifestyle, and other income sources. Use the calculator to compare scenarios rather than relying on one rule of thumb.

faq.q: What's a realistic rate of return for retirement investments?
faq.a: Historical stock market returns average around 10% annually, but a conservative estimate of 6-8% is often used for retirement planning to account for market volatility and a more conservative asset allocation as you approach retirement.

faq.q: When should I start saving for retirement?
faq.a: Starting earlier generally gives savings more time to compound. The calculator can help compare how different starting ages and contribution levels change long-term projections.

faq.q: How much income will I need in retirement?
faq.a: A common rule of thumb is that you'll need 70-90% of your pre-retirement income to maintain your lifestyle in retirement. However, this varies based on your expected expenses, healthcare costs, and desired activities in retirement.
